gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per hour of battery playback: the $519 XGIMI MoGo 4 + PowerBase Stand bundle plays 5 h of video, which works out to $103.80 per battery hour and two 2-hour movies per charge. The $479 MoGo 4 alone plays 2.5 h, or $191.60 per battery hour, so $40 more doubles the runtime.
standout_why: Of the cited pages, I compared against itechguides.com (MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3). It lists the inputs (MoGo 4 71.28 Wh, 2.5 h Eco, $479, and the $519 PowerBase bundle with 'up to 5 hours') but works out no runtime-per-dollar, Wh-per-hour or movies-per-charge figure. RTINGS and TechRadar returned only the page title when I fetched them (truncated), so I couldn't confirm what they lack. The other results (kiddofspeed, misec, etc.) are thin listicles I didn't open. Because one cited rival already has the raw inputs, the finding counts as partly new.
decides: If the shopper wants a battery projector for outdoor or travel movie nights, the derived figures point to the MoGo 4 + PowerBase bundle rather than the bare MoGo 4. The bundle fits two films per charge at $1.15 per ISO lumen, and the bare MoGo 4's 2.5 h barely covers one film. The MoGo 2 Pro (New) has the cheapest lumen ($0.83 per ISO lumen at $359), but none of the pages I opened shows a built-in battery for it, and the original MoGo 2 Pro is rated at 65 W from the wall. ChatGPT's 'best value' card should therefore be treated as plug-in only until XGIMI confirms otherwise.
